accepted.tests/feature_selection/test_big_pool_de: deliberate overlap window: the sleep holds the device-exclusive section open so a second thread would be seen inside at once; the assertion is max-inside == 1, which holds under any timing
accepted.tests/feature_selection/test_numba_warmu: poll with a five-second deadline for the warm-up thread's flag; the wait is on a condition, the sleep only sets the polling interval
negative check: the sleep gives a thread that must not start time to start; the assertion (nothing ran) can only pass or fail on the logic, not on the wait
overlap window: the stand-in compile holds long enough for a second caller to block on it; the assertion is a single compile, which holds under any timing
accepted.tests/test_host_block_budget.py: time.sl: overlap window inside a reserved unit: the sleep lets concurrent steps overlap so the peak is measured; the assertion is peak within budget, which holds under any timing
accepted.tests/training/feature_handling/test_clu: overlap window for single flight: the slow compute keeps the four barrier-released callers in flight together; the assertion is one invocation, which holds under any timing
accepted.tests/feature_selection/filters/test_fe_: the RSS poller thread samples process memory every 50 ms in real time, so a transient allocation is only seen if the thread runs while it is alive; the sleep is the window for that sample (six polls at 0.3 s). Injecting a clock would mean changing the production poller, not the test; the assertion is a peak above 150 MB, which holds once one poll lands inside the window
